topic: The Pi-Collision Paradox: How Counting Collisions Reveals Digits of Pi
target_audience: High school or undergraduate students with an interest in physics and mathematics

sections.title: The Setup: The Elastic Collision Mystery
lecture_lines: Two blocks collide on a frictionless surface.
The smaller block hits the larger one.
The larger block bounces off a wall.
animations: Display two blocks labeled 'm1' and 'm2' in #FFFFFF.
Animate m1 moving right toward m2.
Animate collision between m1 and m2.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Conservation Laws
lecture_lines: Collisions obey momentum and energy conservation.
These laws govern how velocity changes.
Blocks eventually move away from the wall.
animations: Animate blocks moving apart after wall collision.

sections.title: The Scaling Connection: Linking Physics to Geometry
lecture_lines: Mass ratios reveal digits of Pi.
animations: Draw a circle outline representing Pi in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Phase Space Visualization
lecture_lines: Phase space diagrams explain this pattern.
Velocities reflect within a circular arc.
animations: Draw v1 vs v2 axes in #FFFFFF.
Animate a circular arc path in the v1-v2 plane.
Animate point bouncing reflecting along the arc.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Pi exists in discrete physical systems.
Math and physics are deeply unified.
Explore how mass ratios magnify Pi.
